en: to have a talk; to hold a conversation

examples.en: The representatives of the two countries will hold talks tomorrow.
The president held talks with the head of an overseas company.
The reporters waited outside while the talks went on.

examples.ko: 두 회사는 가격 문제로 다시 회담하기로 했어요.
examples.en: The two companies decided to talk again about the price.
The result of the talks will be announced in the afternoon.
We had no time to meet and hold talks.

explain: 나라나 큰 단체의 대표가 공식적으로 만나 이야기할 때 써요. 친구나 동료와 하는 이야기에는 '이야기하다', 회사 일에는 '미팅하다'가 자연스러워요. 보통 '회담을 하다'로 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: The two presidents hold talks tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: '회담하다'보다 이 형태를 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This form is used more often than the single verb 회담하다.

phrases.en: The summit is held in Seoul.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나라의 대표끼리 만나는 큰 회담을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a major meeting between leaders of countries.

phrases.en: The two representatives meet and talk.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쉽게 풀어 쓴 말이에요. 공식적인 느낌은 약해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simpler way to say it, with less of a formal feel.

explain_en: Used when representatives of countries or large organizations meet officially. For friends or colleagues, '이야기하다' is natural, and '미팅하다' for business. People usually say '회담을 하다'.

en: to be turbulent; to be tumultuous

examples.en: These days an unsettling rumor is going around the neighborhood.
As the incidents continued, public sentiment became uneasy.
The mood is so uneasy that I'm afraid to go out at night.
Don't believe the ominous stories that have spread around.
The world feels unsettled, so make sure to lock up well.

examples.ko: 회사가 어렵다는 말에 사무실 분위기가 흉흉해요.
examples.en: After hearing the company is in trouble, the mood in the office is tense.

explain: 소문, 민심, 분위기, 세상처럼 사람들이 불안하고 뒤숭숭할 때 써요. 사람의 성격이나 얼굴을 말하는 말이 아니라 주변 분위기를 말해요.

phrases.example: 사고가 난 뒤로 동네 분위기가 흉흉해요.
phrases.en: Since the accident, the mood in the neighborhood has been uneasy.
phrases.nuance_ko: '흉흉하다'를 '분위기' 앞에 붙여 주변이 불안하고 뒤숭숭한 느낌을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Puts '흉흉하다' before 'mood' to describe an uneasy, unsettled atmosphere around people.

phrases.en: The world feels so unsettled that I'm afraid on the streets at night.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어요'를 붙여 지금 세상이 불안하다고 말하는 해요체 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite '-아/어요' form, used to say that the world feels unsettled right now.

phrases.en: As prices rose, public sentiment became uneasy.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어지다'가 붙어 사람들의 마음이 점점 불안해지는 변화를 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-아/어지다' shows people's mood gradually becoming uneasy.

explain_en: It is used for rumors, public sentiment, mood or the world when people feel anxious and unsettled. It describes the surrounding atmosphere, not a person's character or face.

t90.ax: The world feels unsettled, so make sure to lock up well.

examples.en: I have longed for freedom for a long time.
The child yearned for the parents' love.
People prayed, longing for peace.
The dream I had yearned for finally came true.

examples.ko: 성공을 갈망하는 사람은 쉽게 포기하지 않아요.
examples.en: A person who craves success does not give up easily.
I long for a chance to study in Korea.

explain: '바라다'나 '원하다'보다 훨씬 간절하고 목마른 느낌이에요. 자유·사랑·평화처럼 크고 추상적인 것에 자주 써요. 일상의 물건에는 '갖고 싶다'가 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: My longing for freedom grew bigger and bigger.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사 '갈망하다'의 명사 꼴이고 '~에 대한 갈망'으로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The noun form of 갈망하다, often used as '~에 대한 갈망'.

phrases.en: He longed for success, so he worked day and night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이루고 싶은 큰 목표를 아주 간절히 바랄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for intensely wishing for a big goal you want to achieve.

phrases.en: The dream he had longed for came true.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거부터 계속 바라던 것을 꾸밀 때 '-던'을 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: -던 describes something that was wished for continuously in the past.

explain_en: It is far more intense and thirsty than 바라다 or 원하다. It is often used for big, abstract things such as freedom, love and peace. For everyday objects, 갖고 싶다 sounds more natural.

en: to be elated; to be enhanced

examples.ko: 경기가 끝날 때가 되자 분위기가 고조됐어요.
examples.en: As the game neared its end, the mood heightened.

examples.ko: 두 나라 사이의 긴장이 고조되고 있어요.
examples.en: Tension between the two countries is rising.
When the concert started, the excitement rose to the max.
The emotion swells as the song goes toward its second half.
Interest will rise as the election gets closer.

examples.ko: 갈등이 고조되기 전에 이야기를 해 봐요.
examples.en: Let's talk before the conflict escalates.

explain: 분위기·긴장·감정·관심처럼 눈에 안 보이는 것이 점점 높아질 때 써요. 기대나 흥분 같은 좋은 쪽에도, 긴장이나 갈등 같은 나쁜 쪽에도 써요. 온도나 값이 오를 때는 '오르다'를 써요.

phrases.example: 새 영화에 대한 관심이 점점 고조되고 있어요.
phrases.en: Interest in the new movie is gradually rising.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람들의 관심이 점점 커질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when people's interest keeps growing.

phrases.en: As the announcement date got closer, expectations rose.
phrases.nuance_ko: 좋은 쪽으로 기대나 흥분이 높아질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when hope or excitement builds in a positive way.

phrases.en: The concert began in an excited atmosphere.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ' 형태로 바꿔 명사 앞에 쓰면 이미 높아진 분위기를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past-modifier form describes an atmosphere that has already risen.

explain_en: Used when something intangible like mood, tension, feeling or interest keeps rising. It fits both good things (excitement) and bad ones (tension, conflict). For temperature or prices going up, use '오르다'.

t90.ax: Let's talk before the conflict escalates.

examples.ko: 이 영화는 처음부터 끝까지 긴박감이 넘쳐요.
examples.en: This movie is full of tension from beginning to end.
I could feel the urgency in the breaking news.

examples.ko: 음악 때문에 장면의 긴박감이 더 커졌어요.
examples.en: The music made the sense of urgency in the scene even stronger.
The novel had no suspense, so it was a bit boring.

examples.ko: 구조 현장의 긴박감은 말로 다 설명할 수 없어요.
examples.en: The urgency at the rescue site can't be fully put into words.

examples.ko: 그 소식을 들은 순간 긴박감에 숨이 막혔어요.
examples.en: The moment I heard the news, the urgency took my breath away.

explain: 사건이 급하고 아슬아슬하게 돌아갈 때 느끼는 분위기를 말해요. 영화, 소설, 뉴스, 구조 현장 이야기에서 '긴박감이 넘치다', '긴박감을 주다'처럼 자주 써요. 단순히 바쁜 것은 '바쁘다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: The fast music adds a sense of urgency to the scene.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무엇이 분위기를 급박하게 만든다는 뜻이에요. 사람이나 소리, 연출이 주어가 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means something makes the mood tense and urgent; the subject can be a person, sound, or direction.
phrases.en_equiv: to give a sense of urgency

phrases.en: I could feel the urgency in the voice on the phone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 듣거나 보는 사람이 분위기를 느낄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the listener or viewer senses the urgent mood.

phrases.example: 이 드라마는 긴박감 있는 장면이 계속 이어져요.
phrases.en: This drama keeps going with tense, urgent scenes.
phrases.nuance_ko: '긴박감'이 뒤의 명사를 꾸며 줄 때 쓰는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form used when 긴박감 describes the noun that follows.

explain_en: It describes the tense mood when events are urgent and on a knife edge. It is often used for movies, novels, news and rescue scenes, as in '긴박감이 넘치다' or '긴박감을 주다'. Simply being busy is just '바쁘다'.

t90.ax: I could feel the urgency in the breaking news.

en: to be confused; to be confounded; to be muddled

examples.en: I got an award so suddenly that I was stunned.
I just woke up and I'm still groggy.
He looked at me with a bewildered face.

examples.ko: 갑작스러운 소식에 한동안 어리벙벙해서 말도 못 했어요.
examples.en: I was so stunned by the sudden news that I couldn't speak for a while.
Don't look so confused; try explaining slowly.

examples.ko: 길을 잘못 들어 어리벙벙한 채로 서 있었어요.
examples.en: I took a wrong turn and stood there confused.

explain: 놀라거나 상황을 잘 몰라서 멍해진 상태예요. '어리둥절하다'와 비슷하고, 잠이 덜 깨서 정신이 흐릿할 때도 써요.

phrases.en: He stood there with a bewildered look.
phrases.nuance_ko: 멍하고 어리둥절한 얼굴을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a blank, bewildered face.

phrases.en: Everyone looked dazed at the sudden news.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉으로 멍하고 어리둥절해 보일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone visibly looks dazed and confused.

phrases.en: I was confused when they suddenly called my name.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어리벙벙하다와 비슷하지만 잠이 덜 깬 느낌은 적어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 어리벙벙하다 but without the feel of being half asleep.

explain_en: It describes being dazed from surprise or not understanding a situation. It is similar to '어리둥절하다' and can also be used when you're groggy from sleep.

en: to be full; to be filled; to be overflowing

examples.en: My heart is filled with happiness.
I want to spend a fulfilling day.
I was so full of confidence that I wasn't nervous.
The concert hall was filled with excitement.
I feel a heart full of gratitude.
When I'm full of joy, I start singing.

explain: 충만하다는 행복, 자신감, 기쁨, 사랑처럼 눈에 안 보이는 감정이나 기운에 써요. 컵에 물이 가득한 건 '가득하다'나 '차다'를 써요. 보통 '~으로 충만하다'로 말해요.

phrases.en: It's the day before the exam, but I'm full of confidence.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자신감이 아주 가득할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This phrase is used when someone is full of confidence.

phrases.en: My heart feels full when I listen to music.
phrases.nuance_ko: 점점 가득 차는 변화를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is used for a gradual change toward feeling full.

phrases.en: My heart is full of joy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 말이고 일상에서 더 쉽게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is a similar word and easier to use in everyday speech.

explain_en: 충만하다 is for invisible feelings and energy such as happiness, confidence, joy, and love. A cup full of water is 가득하다 or 차다. It usually appears as '~으로 충만하다'.

t90.ax: I want to spend a fulfilling day.

en: to be peaceful; to be not ill

examples.en: My mind is at peace these days.
My parents are doing well and at ease.
Have a peaceful night.

examples.ko: 시골에서 사니까 훨씬 평안하게 지낼 수 있어요.
examples.en: Living in the countryside, I can live much more peacefully.
His expression looked very peaceful.
After praying, my heart became calm.

explain: '평안하다'는 큰 걱정이나 문제가 없이 마음이 가라앉은 상태예요. '편하다'보다 격식 있고 조용한 느낌이에요. 편지나 인사말에서 '평안하시길 바랍니다', 교회에서 '평안을 빕니다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: When I pray, I feel a peaceful mind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에 붙여 마음이나 하루가 조용하고 편안하다고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Placed before a noun to describe a calm mind or day.

phrases.en: Grandmother, please always be well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 윗사람에게 안녕을 비는 정중한 인사말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite greeting wishing well-being to someone older.

phrases.en: My mind is not at peace because the exam is near.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음이 불안하거나 편치 않을 때 부정형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Negative form for when one feels uneasy.

explain_en: 평안하다 describes a calm state with no big worries or problems. It feels more formal and quiet than 편하다. It is used in letters and greetings, such as 평안하시길 바랍니다, and in churches as 평안을 빕니다.

dis.h: worry-free, at ease; safe and sound
gh: calm place or scene, without conflict

p.n: 평안 stresses being free of worry; 평화 stresses calm and no conflict.

examples.ko: 올림픽 개회식은 저녁 여덟 시에 시작해요.
examples.en: The Olympic opening ceremony starts at eight in the evening.

examples.ko: 영화제 개회식에 유명한 배우들이 많이 왔어요.
examples.en: Many famous actors came to the film festival's opening ceremony.
The representative gave a greeting speech at the opening ceremony.

examples.ko: 비가 와서 개회식이 한 시간 늦어졌어요.
examples.en: It rained, so the opening ceremony was delayed an hour.

examples.ko: 우리 학교 체육대회 개회식은 운동장에서 열려요.
examples.en: Our school's sports day opening ceremony is held on the field.
I cheered while watching the opening ceremony on TV.

explain: 반대말은 '폐회식'이에요. 올림픽, 영화제, 체육대회처럼 규모가 있는 행사에 써요. '개회식에 참석하다', '개회식을 열다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: The film festival opening ceremony takes place next week.
phrases.nuance_ko: '개회식'과 비슷하고 영화제나 공연, 축제에 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 'gaehoesik', more common for film festivals, shows, and festivals.

phrases.en: The president also attended the opening ceremony.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행사에 직접 가서 함께할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone goes in person to take part in the event.

phrases.en: The competition holds its opening ceremony tomorrow morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행사를 여는 쪽에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the perspective of the people holding the event.

explain_en: The opposite is 폐회식 (closing ceremony). It is used for sizable events such as the Olympics, film festivals, and sports days. You say 개회식에 참석하다 or 개회식을 열다.

t90.ax: I cheered while watching the opening ceremony on TV.

examples.en: In the military, saluting a superior is basic.
The soldiers saluted the flag all at once.
The students bowed to the teacher and sat down.

examples.ko: 경찰관이 지나가던 어르신께 경례해서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: A police officer saluted an elderly person passing by, which surprised me.
When the commander arrives, everyone has to salute.

examples.ko: 아들이 거울 앞에서 멋있게 경례해 보고 있어요.
examples.en: My son is trying out a cool salute in front of the mirror.

explain: 군대, 학교 조회, 경찰처럼 정해진 동작이나 구호로 예의를 표할 때 써요. 일상에서 만나는 인사에는 '인사하다'를 쓰고, 경례하다는 쓰지 않아요. 윗사람에게는 '~께 경례하다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: The students salute the flag.
phrases.nuance_ko: '경례하다'와 같은 뜻으로 명사 '경례'를 써서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 경례하다, using the noun 경례.

phrases.en: The soldier gave a hand salute to the officer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 손을 들어 올려서 하는 군대식 경례를 뜻해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A military salute made by raising the hand.

phrases.en: The general received the soldiers' salute.
phrases.nuance_ko: 경례를 받는 윗사람 입장에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the viewpoint of the superior receiving the salute.

explain_en: It is used for showing respect with a set gesture or call, as in the military, school assemblies or the police. For everyday greetings you use '인사하다', not 경례하다. To a superior you say '~께 경례하다'.

examples.en: The fridge is full of food.
Every plate was piled full of food.
His eyes were brimming with tears.

examples.ko: 창고에 쌀이 그득한 걸 보니 마음이 든든해요.
examples.en: Seeing the warehouse packed with rice makes me feel secure.

examples.ko: 상 위에 반찬이 그득해서 어디서부터 먹을지 고민했어요.
examples.en: The table was so full of side dishes that I wondered where to start.

examples.ko: 장바구니가 그득하지 않아서 다시 마트에 갔어요.
examples.en: The shopping bag wasn't full, so I went back to the store.

explain: '가득하다'와 거의 같은 뜻이지만 풍성하게 차 있는 느낌이 있어요. 'N이 그득하다'처럼 음식, 물건, 눈물, 소리 등에 써요. '그득', '그득히' 같은 부사도 있어요.

phrases.en: I received a basket full of fruit as a gift.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸며 주는 형태로, 풍성하게 찬 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form before a noun, describing something richly full.

phrases.example: 슬픈 이야기를 듣고 눈에 눈물이 그득했어요.
phrases.en: After hearing the sad story, my eyes were full of tears.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈에 눈물이 가득 찬 모습을 나타낼 때 이렇게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is how you describe eyes filled with tears.

phrases.en: I filled the bowl with rice.
phrases.nuance_ko: '그득히'는 가득 차게 하는 동작과 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adverb '그득히' goes with the action of filling something up.

explain_en: It means almost the same as '가득하다' but gives a feeling of abundance. It is used as 'N이 그득하다' with food, things, tears, sounds, and so on. There are also adverbs '그득' and '그득히'.

t90.ax: The fridge is full of food.

examples.en: Clothes and socks are lying all over the floor.

examples.ko: 태풍이 지난 뒤 길에 쓰레기가 나뒹굴고 있었어요.
examples.en: After the typhoon, trash was strewn around the street.
On Sunday I spent the day lazing about on the sofa.

examples.ko: 책상 밑에 빈 페트병이 나뒹구는 걸 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw an empty plastic bottle lying around under the desk.
The ball rolled off and lay about on the field.
The kids tumble around playing on the lawn.

explain: 물건이 여기저기 굴러다니며 널려 있는 모습에 가장 잘 써요. 사람이 뒹굴뒹굴 누워서 편하게 또는 게으르게 지내는 모습에도 써요. 'ㄹ' 받침이 빠져 '나뒹구는', '나뒹구니까'가 되는 것에 주의하세요.

phrases.example: 책상 밑에 연필이 여러 개 나뒹굴어요.
phrases.en: Several pencils are lying scattered under the desk.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건이 흩어져 있는 모습을 말하는 해요체 활용이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite form for describing things lying scattered around.

phrases.en: I picked up the trash scattered around the park.
phrases.nuance_ko: 'ㄹ' 받침이 빠진 꾸미는 말로, 뒤의 명사를 꾸며요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifying form with the ㄹ dropped, describing a noun.

phrases.en: Toys are lying all over the floor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 장소와 함께 써서 어디에 널려 있는지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Combined with a place to say where things are strewn.
phrases.en_equiv: to lie around on the floor

explain_en: It fits best for things lying scattered and rolling around. It can also describe a person lazing about, lying around comfortably or lazily. Note that the 'ㄹ' drops before some endings, giving '나뒹구는' and '나뒹구니까'.

t90.ax: The kids tumble around playing on the lawn.

examples.en: The fishermen came back with full catches, so the port is bustling.
We caught a lot of fish today, so the boat is full.

examples.ko: 아버지는 매번 만선이 되기를 바라며 바다로 나가세요.
examples.en: My father goes out to sea every time hoping for a full catch.
The boat returned filled with the joy of a full catch.

examples.ko: 마을 사람들은 올해도 만선을 빌며 제사를 지냈어요.
examples.en: The villagers held a ritual wishing for a full catch again this year.

examples.ko: 만선 깃발을 단 배들이 줄지어 들어와요.
examples.en: Boats flying full-catch flags are coming in one after another.

explain: 고기를 가득 싣고 돌아온 배, 또는 그런 상태를 말해요. 어부들이 '만선의 꿈'이라고 하듯이 바람을 담아 쓰는 일도 많아요. 고기를 못 잡고 돌아오면 '빈손으로 돌아오다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: Today the boat came back fully loaded.
phrases.nuance_ko: 배가 고기로 가득 찬 상태가 되었다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the boat has become full of fish.

phrases.example: 어부들은 만선의 꿈을 안고 바다로 나가요.
phrases.en: The fishermen head out to sea dreaming of a full catch.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바람을 담아 말할 때 쓰는 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing used when expressing a hope.

phrases.en: We caught no fish and came back empty-handed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 만선의 반대 상황을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the opposite situation of 만선.

explain_en: It means a boat that comes back loaded with fish, or that state itself. It is often used with hope, as in '만선의 꿈' (the dream of a full catch). If the boat returns with nothing, people say '빈손으로 돌아오다'.

examples.ko: 행사장 장막 안에서 사람들이 따뜻한 차를 마시고 있어요.
examples.en: People are drinking warm tea inside the tent at the event site.

examples.ko: 두꺼운 장막을 걷으니 아침 햇살이 들어왔어요.
examples.en: When I pulled back the thick curtain, the morning sunlight came in.
The fog covered the village like a curtain.

examples.ko: 비밀의 장막에 가려져 있던 사실이 드러났어요.
examples.en: A fact that had been hidden behind a veil of secrecy came to light.

examples.ko: 무대 장막 뒤에서 배우들이 숨을 고르고 있어요.
examples.en: Behind the stage curtain, the actors are catching their breath.

examples.ko: 무대의 장막이 천천히 올라가자 박수가 터졌어요.
examples.en: As the stage curtain slowly rose, applause broke out.

explain: 창문에 다는 '커튼'과 달리 크고 무거운 천으로 공간을 가리거나 나눌 때 써요. '안개의 장막', '비밀의 장막'처럼 무언가를 가리는 것을 비유할 때도 많아요. 임시로 치는 큰 텐트는 일상에서 '천막'이라고 해요.

phrases.example: 냉전 시기에는 철의 장막 때문에 동서 유럽의 교류가 어려웠어요.
phrases.en: During the Cold War, exchange between Eastern and Western Europe was difficult because of the Iron Curtain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 냉전 시기 서유럽과 동유럽 사이를 가른 보이지 않는 경계를 가리켜요. 역사 수업이나 뉴스에서 볼 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: It refers to the invisible boundary that divided Western and Eastern Europe during the Cold War. You can see it in history classes and the news.

explain_en: Unlike '커튼' hung on windows, it is a large, heavy cloth used to hide or divide a space. It is also often used figuratively for something that hides things, as in '안개의 장막' and '비밀의 장막'. A large temporary tent is called '천막' in daily talk.
